plan.premise: In this clearly fictional romance, football superstar Neymar arrives at a small São Paulo café with a reputation shaped by headlines and a habit of expecting others to accommodate him. Isa, a proud waitress working to keep her family afloat, dislikes celebrities and refuses to flatter him. When a sudden media commotion threatens the café staff, Neymar must decide whether to protect his image or help the people caught in the disruption. Their sharp exchanges give way, slowly and unevenly, to trust and love.
plan.audience: Adult readers who enjoy concise, illustrated celebrity romance and enemies-to-lovers stories.

chapters.title: A Table by the Window
chapters.summary: Isa's shift at a modest neighborhood café is disrupted when Neymar arrives with an entourage and expects the room to bend around him. Their first exchange establishes her contempt for celebrity entitlement and his surprise at being treated like an ordinary difficult customer.
keyBeats: Introduce Isa balancing a busy shift with concern about rent and her family's needs.
Introduce fictional Neymar arriving at the café, distracted by attention and impatient with ordinary service.
Isa refuses a special demand and tells him plainly that fame does not make him the only person in the room.

chapters.title: The Café in the Headlines
chapters.summary: A crowd gathers outside after Neymar is recognized, and phones turn the café into a spectacle. Isa and Neymar disagree over how to manage the interruption, then cooperate to get staff and customers safely through the rush.
keyBeats: A fictional burst of online attention brings photographers and curious onlookers to the café entrance.
Neymar initially focuses on leaving without looking bad, while Isa prioritizes the staff and customers.
He follows Isa's practical plan, helping clear a safe route without asking for praise or a photograph.

chapters.title: A Favor Without a Camera
chapters.summary: After the crowd disperses, the café faces a costly mess and a lost evening's business. Neymar offers help in a way that initially sounds like a public-relations fix; Isa challenges him to make a useful choice without turning the staff into props.
keyBeats: The café owner counts the disruption's concrete costs while Isa helps her coworkers clean and reopen.
Neymar proposes a conspicuous gesture, and Isa explains why the workers need practical support rather than publicity.
He arranges discreet, immediate help through the owner and accepts Isa's refusal to perform gratitude for him.

chapters.title: The Story Everyone Wants
chapters.summary: A misleading headline about the café fuels fresh attention and puts Isa's job and privacy at risk. Neymar can let the rumor run for convenience, but chooses to correct the public account without naming Isa or using her image.
keyBeats: A fictional headline distorts the café incident and brings unwanted attention back to Isa's workplace.
Isa tells Neymar she will not be made into a supporting character in his public image.
Neymar issues a clear correction that takes responsibility for his part and keeps Isa's identity and private life out of it.

chapters.title: A Quiet Table for Two
chapters.summary: With the café back to its ordinary rhythm, Neymar returns without an entourage and asks Isa to speak with him after her shift. She names what she still distrusts; he listens without bargaining. Isa decides to give him a chance, and they leave together on terms she has chosen.
keyBeats: Neymar returns alone and waits until Isa has finished her work before asking for her time.
Isa describes the limits she needs, and Neymar answers with listening and accountability rather than a grand promise.
Isa chooses a modest first date, and Neymar follows her lead as they step into the evening together.

At the Mercado Municipal de São Paulo, the fruit stalls begin to look different after the lunch rush, when bruised peaches sit beside immaculate pyramids of oranges. Dona Célia, who has sold produce there for twenty years, keeps a small knife under the counter and cuts samples only when a customer asks. Her hands move quickly, but she never hurries a child choosing between two slices of mango.

On Rua Avanhandava, a restaurant's back door opens onto a narrow lane where delivery crates collect before dawn. Paulo, the cook at the corner trattoria, knows which crate belongs to which supplier by the color of its twine. He writes the day's shortages on the back of a receipt and pins it beside the stove. At six, the owner reads the note while the espresso machine sputters awake.

In Recife, a bus driver named Lúcia keeps a folded paper timetable in her shirt pocket, though her route now appears on a screen above the dashboard. She checks the paper at the last stop, where a schoolboy named Davi often waits with a cello case nearly as tall as he is. One rainy Tuesday, Lúcia held the doors while he tucked the case under the seat. The bus left two minutes late, and Davi reached his music lesson with dry strings.

draft.title: A Tray Between Them
draft.markdown:
Three coffees rocked on Isa’s tray as she threaded between the close-set tables at Café Aurora. At the front window, a man in dark sunglasses gestured toward the occupied seats. “Could you clear this area?” he asked. “I need some space.”

Isa set the coffees down, steadying each cup. “Those tables are for customers,” she said. “Not reputations.”

He lowered his sunglasses. It was Neymar, the football star in this fictional encounter. His gaze moved over the crowded room. A couple at the next table whispered; around them, spoons tapped cups and Rosa called an order from the counter.

Isa tucked the empty tray beneath her arm and turned back to her customers. Neymar’s hand, still lifted toward the window tables, dropped to his side. He stood amid the lunch-hour noise, with every seat still occupied.
